rationale: Start with a broad gradient to observe all 10 compounds and locate their elution window while minimizing early co-elution. The retention pattern will guide window trimming and identify critical pairs for subsequent slope and temperature optimization.

Keep the gradient unchanged and raise temperature to test selectivity at the sole under-resolved pair (R = 0.82). This should shorten retention while potentially resolving that pair without sacrificing the other separations.

The central peak pattern suggests an elution-order reversal between 40 and 50 C, so 55 C may separate the crossed pair beyond R = 1.5. This intermediate step also limits further compression of the neighboring pair whose resolution decreased at 50 C.

Injection 3 already achieved the maximum CRF and remains the best method. Test a shorter gradient to see whether run time can be reduced while maintaining R ≥ 1.5, particularly for the two marginally resolved pairs.

Shift the starting organic fraction upward while preserving injection 3’s gradient slope, aiming to shorten retention without the resolution loss caused by injection 4’s steeper gradient. The first peak’s estimated elution fraction was about 0.10, so this also tests whether early retention remains adequate.

Injection 3 already attains the maximum score; this run explores a lower-temperature selectivity regime for a shorter fully resolved method. Keeping injection 4’s gradient unchanged isolates temperature effects and tests whether the central peak cluster separates on the opposite side of its order reversals.

Keep injection 3 as the maximum-score fallback while testing a substantially faster method. A hotter, steeper gradient may carry the limiting pair through an elution-order reversal into renewed separation, though neighboring pairs may become compressed.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 3 to improve the marginal separation that deteriorated with steeper gradients, while keeping the last peak within 10 minutes. Monitor the other critical pair, whose resolution showed little slope sensitivity.

Combine higher temperature to strengthen the nearly slope-insensitive critical separation with a shallower gradient to recover resolution of its neighboring pair. This targets a maximum-score method with more separation margin, while aiming to keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Use a shallower slope than injection 5 to recover its limiting separation, while retaining the higher starting organic fraction that improved the other critical pair. This targets full resolution with better minimum-resolution margin and a last-peak time near injection 3’s.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope from injection 10 to lift its limiting R = 1.47 above 1.5. The other critical pair should retain its separation, and the last peak is expected comfortably before 10 minutes.

Set the slope between injections 10 and 11, targeting full resolution with a shorter last-peak time than injection 11. Their results predict both critical pairs just above R = 1.5, with all peaks eluting during the gradient.

Explore a faster alternative to the maximum-score methods by combining a higher starting organic fraction with a gentler slope than injection 7. These changes may rebalance its two under-resolved central pairs while preserving the short retention times at 60 C.

Raise the starting organic fraction to test whether the remaining central overlap in injection 13 separates further on the reversed-order branch. Monitor the first pair closely, since its resolution may become limiting as early retention decreases.

Explore a cooler, faster-gradient selectivity regime that may separate the central cluster on the opposite side of its temperature-driven order reversals. Retain the low starting organic fraction to protect early separation; the maximum-score methods remain available as fallbacks.

Seek greater resolution margin than the existing maximum-score methods by pairing a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient. The higher start may strengthen the slope-insensitive critical pair, while the shallower slope compensates for compression of its neighbor; monitor early separation and the 10-minute cutoff.

Slightly flatten injection 16’s gradient to bring its sole deficient pair above R = 1.5. Its other critical pair has useful margin at R = 1.74, and the expected last-peak time remains below 10 minutes.

Test whether a shallower gradient resolves the crowded central cluster at 35 C, where the short gradient performed poorly. This explores a cooler alternative to the maximum-score 55 C methods, with the last peak estimated near but below 10 minutes.

Slightly reduce the slope relative to injection 17 to improve its R = 1.63 limiting pair while preserving the neighboring separation. This targets a larger minimum-resolution margin at the maximum CRF, with the last peak expected before 10 minutes.

Trim injection 3’s gradient endpoint while preserving its starting composition, temperature, and exact slope. Because all peaks should elute before the shortened gradient ends, this should retain CRF = 1.000 with a shorter programmed gradient and lower final organic fraction.

Further trim the successful gradient while preserving its exact slope and temperature. The last peak’s estimated elution fraction is about 0.57, below the new endpoint, so all separations should remain unchanged with an eight-minute programmed gradient.

Trim injection 11 to an eight-minute gradient while preserving its slope and its better minimum resolution of 1.58. The last peak is expected before the gradient reaches the outlet endpoint at 8.65 minutes, so the maximum CRF should be retained.

Use a slope between injections 17 and 19 to target a minimum resolution near 1.7 while retaining the maximum CRF. The trimmed endpoint should still accommodate the last peak during the gradient, with elution expected around 9.3 minutes.

Preserve the successful gradient slope through the first nine peaks, then test whether a lower-organic hold elutes the isolated final peak before 10 minutes. This could retain the maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient and lower final organic fraction, although the last peak will likely elute later.

Preserve injection 19’s slope and improved minimum resolution of 1.69, but end the gradient earlier and elute the isolated final peak during the hold. This tests a shorter programmed gradient with greater separation margin than injection 24; the remaining risk is whether the last peak stays within 10 minutes.
